```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import sys
from pathlib import Path
import os

PROJ_ROOT = Path("..").resolve()
if str(PROJ_ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(PROJ_ROOT))
os.chdir(PROJ_ROOT)

import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import src.cleaning as c, src.charts as ch
import importlib
importlib.reload(c); importlib.reload(ch)

from src.cleaning import (
    load_usviber_combined, load_fred_employment,
    load_bea, load_nps_annual,
)
from src.charts import PALETTE

tour     = load_usviber_combined()
fred     = load_fred_employment()
bea_real = load_bea("2.3")
viis_ann = load_nps_annual("VIIS")

fred_ann = (
    fred.groupby("year")["emp_sa"].mean()
    .reset_index().rename(columns={"emp_sa": "emp_sa_avg"})
)
af_real = (
    bea_real[bea_real["label"].str.contains("ccommodation", case=False, na=False)]
    .drop_duplicates(subset="year")[["year", "value"]]
    .rename(columns={"value": "af_real"})
)

BASE = 2016

def _index(df, year_col, val_col, base=BASE):
    bv = df.loc[df[year_col] == base, val_col]
    if bv.empty or bv.values[0] == 0:
        return None
    base_val = bv.values[0]
    out = df[[year_col, val_col]].copy()
    out["idx"] = out[val_col] / base_val * 100
    return out
```



## Context

In September 2017, Hurricanes Irma and Maria struck the U.S. Virgin Islands within two weeks of each other. The territory took a direct hit from two Category 5 storms, destroying hotel infrastructure, damaging or closing Virgin Islands National Park, and disrupting the economy that tourism had sustained for decades. Three years later, before recovery was complete, COVID-19 closed borders and halted cruise shipping.

This study draws on data spanning roughly 25 years across six primary sources to document how the USVI tourism economy has moved through those shocks — and what recovery looks like in 2024 and 2025. Source coverage varies: USVIBER provides annual data from 2000, with 2001–2009 from an earlier publication vintage and 2010–2024 from the current edition; FRED employment begins in 1990; BEA data run 2002–2021/2022.

One headline stands out: **total visitor arrivals have nearly returned to their 2016 level, but the composition has shifted fundamentally. Overnight visitors, who generate substantially higher per-trip expenditure than same-day visitors, remain at roughly half their pre-hurricane baseline. Total air arrivals have recovered past their 2016 level, but that recovery is concentrated in same-day air excursionists — the overnight segment of air travel has not recovered in step.**



## The two shocks

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-total-arrivals
#| fig-cap: "Air visitors (all USVI arrivals by air) versus cruise passengers. Total visitors shown as context. COVID virtually halted cruise shipping while air arrivals declined less sharply. 2001–2009 from USVIBER 2010 publication."

fig = go.Figure()
for col, name, color, dash in [
    ("air_visitors",    "Air visitors (reported total)", PALETTE["air_visitors"], "solid"),
    ("cruise_passengers","Cruise passengers",             PALETTE["cruise"],       "dash"),
    ("total_visitors",  "Total visitors",                PALETTE["total"],        "dot"),
]:
    sub = tour[["year", col]].dropna()
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=sub["year"], y=sub[col],
        mode="lines+markers", name=name,
        line=dict(color=color, width=2.5, dash=dash),
        marker=dict(size=5),
    ))

for x_val, label in [(2017, "Irma & Maria"), (2020, "COVID-19")]:
    fig.add_vline(x=x_val, line=dict(color="#aaa", width=1.5, dash="dash"),
                  annotation_text=label, annotation_position="top",
                  annotation_font=dict(size=11, color="#666"))

fig.update_layout(title="Air Visitors vs. Cruise Passengers",
    yaxis_title="Visitors (thousands)",
    height=440,
    margin=dict(l=60, r=30, t=60, b=50),
    annotations=[dict(xref="paper", yref="paper", x=0, y=-0.10,
        text="<span style='color:#888;font-size:11px'>Sources: USVIBER Annual Tourism Indicator 2024; 2001–2009 from USVIBER Annual Tourism Indicators 2010</span>",
        showarrow=False, xanchor="left")],
)
ch.save_fig(fig, "total-arrivals", formats=("png",))
fig.show()
```

The 2017 hurricane shock cut total arrivals to 76% of their 2016 level within the same calendar year — notable given that the storms struck in September, meaning the first eight months of 2017 were largely normal. By 2018, the decline deepened as the full damage to hotel inventory became apparent.

COVID-19 in 2020 produced a collapse of different character: cruise shipping stopped almost entirely (cruise passengers fell to 25% of their 2019 level), while overnight tourists declined less sharply (to about 32% of 2019). The territory's isolation and the absence of large-group gatherings may have made it modestly attractive to small-party leisure travelers once borders reopened.



## A recovery that isn't what it looks like

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-recovery-index
#| fig-cap: "Recovery index, 2016 = 100. Air visitors and cruise passengers are the primary arrival-mode comparison. Overnight tourists show the largest remaining deficit."

series = {
    "Air visitors":          _index(tour, "year", "air_visitors"),
    "Cruise passengers":     _index(tour, "year", "cruise_passengers"),
    "Overnight tourists":    _index(tour, "year", "tourists"),
    "Hotel rooms (USVIBER)": _index(tour, "year", "hotel_rooms"),
    "L&H employment (FRED)": _index(fred_ann, "year", "emp_sa_avg"),
    "A&F real value added":  _index(af_real, "year", "af_real"),
    "VIIS NP visits":        _index(viis_ann.query("year >= 2000"), "year", "recreation_visitors"),
}
styles = {
    "Air visitors":          (PALETTE["air_visitors"], "solid",    2.5),
    "Cruise passengers":     (PALETTE["cruise"],       "solid",    2.5),
    "Overnight tourists":    (PALETTE["tourists"],     "dash",     2),
    "Hotel rooms (USVIBER)": (PALETTE["rooms"],        "dot",      1.5),
    "L&H employment (FRED)": (PALETTE["employment"],   "longdash", 1.5),
    "A&F real value added":  (PALETTE["value_added"],  "dash",     1.5),
    "VIIS NP visits":        (PALETTE["nps_viis"],     "dashdot",  1.5),
}

fig = go.Figure()
for name, df in series.items():
    if df is None:
        continue
    color, dash, width = styles[name]
    sub = df[["year", "idx"]].dropna()
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=sub["year"], y=sub["idx"],
        mode="lines", name=name,
        line=dict(color=color, dash=dash, width=width),
    ))

fig.add_hline(y=100, line=dict(color="#ccc", width=1, dash="dot"),
              annotation_text="2016 = 100", annotation_position="right",
              annotation_font=dict(size=10, color="#999"))
for x_val, label in [(2017, "Irma & Maria"), (2020, "COVID-19")]:
    fig.add_vline(x=x_val, line=dict(color="#aaa", width=1.5, dash="dash"),
                  annotation_text=label, annotation_position="top",
                  annotation_font=dict(size=11, color="#666"))

fig.update_layout(title="Recovery Index (2016 = 100)",
    xaxis=dict(range=[2012, tour["year"].max()]),
    yaxis=dict(range=[0, 120]),
    yaxis_title="Index (2016 = 100)",
    height=480,
    legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="top", y=-0.22, xanchor="center", x=0.5,
        bgcolor="rgba(255,255,255,0)", font=dict(size=11), entrywidthmode="pixels",
        entrywidth=125,),
    margin=dict(l=60, r=30, t=65, b=125),
    annotations=[dict(xref="paper", yref="paper", x=0, y=-0.10,
        text="<span style='color:#888;font-size:11px'>Sources: USVIBER, FRED, BEA, NPS IRMA — author calculations</span>",
        showarrow=False, xanchor="left")],
)
ch.save_fig(fig, "recovery-index", formats=("png",))
fig.show()
```

As of 2024, the index looks deceptively healthy at the top line. Total arrivals sit at 97% of their 2016 baseline. But that recovery in total arrivals masks a stark difference in visitor value. USVIBER data for 2024 imply an average of approximately $2,350 per overnight tourist trip, compared with roughly $450 per cruise passenger stop and roughly $400 per air excursionist — both in nominal 2024 dollars. These are implied averages per arrival in their respective categories, not daily spending estimates.

Air visitors — USVIBER's reported total of all arrivals by air — reached **109% of their 2016 level** by 2024. Cruise passengers reached **90% of their 2016 level**. These two arrival-mode series have followed divergent trajectories since 2017. Within the air total, overnight tourists drove the air recovery before 2017 but have not recovered since: in 2024 they stood at **57% of their 2016 level**, while air excursionists (same-day air arrivals) have grown substantially. Employment and accommodation capacity, measured in hotel rooms, tell a compatible story: the sector is operating at roughly 80–90% of its pre-storm scale, but on a visitor base that has not recovered.



## What the park shows

Virgin Islands National Park on St. John covers roughly 60 percent of the island's land area. Its visitation has followed a markedly different trajectory than territory-wide overnight tourist arrivals, making the two series an interesting comparative indicator — though they measure different things and cannot be treated as equivalent.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-viis-vs-tourists
#| fig-cap: "VIIS NP visitation vs. overnight tourists (both indexed to 2016 = 100). The park's steep decline after 2017 reflects both the hurricane damage to trails and facilities and the collapse in overnight tourism. Its recovery to and past the 2016 level by 2024 is an unresolved divergence from the broader overnight tourist count."

viis_idx = _index(viis_ann.query("year >= 2000"), "year", "recreation_visitors")
tour_idx = _index(tour, "year", "tourists")

fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=viis_idx["year"], y=viis_idx["idx"],
    mode="lines+markers", name="VIIS NP recreation visits",
    line=dict(color=PALETTE["nps_viis"], width=2.5),
    marker=dict(size=5),
))
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=tour_idx["year"], y=tour_idx["idx"],
    mode="lines+markers", name="Overnight tourists (USVIBER)",
    line=dict(color=PALETTE["tourists"], width=2.5, dash="dash"),
    marker=dict(size=5),
))
fig.add_hline(y=100, line=dict(color="#ccc", width=1, dash="dot"),
              annotation_text="2016 = 100", annotation_position="right",
              annotation_font=dict(size=10, color="#999"))
for x_val, label in [(2017, "Irma & Maria"), (2020, "COVID-19")]:
    fig.add_vline(x=x_val, line=dict(color="#aaa", width=1.5, dash="dash"),
                  annotation_text=label, annotation_position="top",
                  annotation_font=dict(size=11, color="#666"))

fig.update_layout(
    title="VIIS NP Visitation vs. Overnight Tourists",
    yaxis_title="Index (2016 = 100)",
    height=420,
    margin=dict(l=60, r=30, t=40, b=50),
    annotations=[dict(xref="paper", yref="paper", x=0, y=-0.10,
        text="<span style='color:#888;font-size:11px'>Sources: NPS IRMA Public Use Statistics; USVIBER Annual Tourism Indicator 2024</span>",
        showarrow=False, xanchor="left")],
)
ch.save_fig(fig, "viis-np-recreation-visits", formats=("png",))
fig.show()
```

VIIS NP visitation reached 103% of its 2016 level in 2024 and 115% in 2025. Overnight tourists, by USVIBER's count, remained at 57% of 2016. The divergence is substantial enough to warrant investigation. Possible explanations include: changes in how NPS counts day-use visitors, increased use of the park by short-term rental guests (not counted as hotel tourists), or different recovery trajectories across segments of the overnight market. This is an open analytical question, not a resolved finding.



## Accommodation capacity

```{python}
#| label: fig-rooms-employment

    line=dict(color=PALETTE["rooms"], width=2.5),

))
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(

for x_val, label in [(2017, "Irma & Maria"), (2020, "COVID-19")]:
    fig.add_vline(x=x_val, line=dict(color="#aaa", width=1.5, dash="dash"),
                  annotation_text=label, annotation_position="top",
                  annotation_font=dict(size=11, color="#666"))

fig.update_layout(

    xaxis=dict(range=[2000, tour["year"].max()]),

    annotations=[dict(xref="paper", yref="paper", x=0, y=-0.10,

        showarrow=False, xanchor="left")],

ch.save_fig(fig, "accommodation-capacity-lh-employment", formats=("png",))
fig.show()
```

Hotel room inventory tracked by USVIBER's annual survey stood at 82% of its 2016 level by 2024. The U.S. Census Economic Census (which counts only payroll-filing establishments) shows a more severe contraction: 2,039 rooms in 2022 versus a 2012 peak of 5,027 — a 59% decline. The Census and USVIBER series use different methodologies and should not be directly compared, but they agree on the direction: accommodation capacity has not recovered.

Leisure and Hospitality employment (FRED, seasonally adjusted) ran at 91% of its 2016 annual average in 2024 — closer to baseline than hotel rooms. This may reflect leaner staffing in surviving hotels, or expanded employment in the food and entertainment segment that comprises a large share of the L&H aggregate.

**A note on hotel occupancy:** USVIBER reports a 2024 occupancy rate of 66.3%, the highest in the available annual series since at least 2000. High occupancy on a reduced room base means the remaining hotels are operating at high utilization; it does not, by itself, establish their financial performance, since room rates, operating costs, and revenue data are not available. This pattern is consistent with either intensive use of surviving capacity, or with constrained supply relative to demand — or both.



## What the broader economy shows

Aggregate GDP and tourism activity tell different stories about the post-hurricane economy. BEA data show that USVI real GDP remained relatively stable in 2017 and grew in 2018–2021, even as visitor arrivals and accommodation revenue remained severely depressed. BEA attributed some of this growth to government spending and private fixed investment, which likely reflect hurricane response and reconstruction activity. These patterns illustrate how economic production can recover through activity outside the visitor economy while tourism itself remains impaired. This analysis does not estimate the contribution of federal disaster assistance to GDP.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-af-gdp-share
#| fig-cap: "Accommodation and food services as a share of USVI nominal GDP, 2002–2021 (BEA data). The sector's GDP share fell from roughly 13% in 2015 to 6% in 2020 before rebounding to 11% in 2021. Important caveat: Accommodation and food services value added is not equivalent to tourism GDP — it includes resident consumption and excludes tourism-related retail, transportation, and recreation."

bea_nom  = load_bea("2.1")
bea_gdp  = load_bea("1.1")

def _get(df, pattern):
    return (df[df["label"].str.contains(pattern, case=False, na=False)]
              .drop_duplicates(subset="year").sort_values("year"))

gdp_nom = _get(bea_gdp, "Gross domestic product")
af_nom  = _get(bea_nom, "Accommodation")
share   = af_nom[["year", "value"]].merge(
    gdp_nom[["year", "value"]].rename(columns={"value": "gdp"}), on="year"
)
share["pct"] = (share["value"] / share["gdp"] * 100).round(1)

fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=share["year"], y=share["pct"],
    mode="lines+markers", name="A&F share of GDP (%)",
    line=dict(color=PALETTE["value_added"], width=2.5),
    fill="tozeroy", fillcolor="rgba(26,79,114,0.08)",
    marker=dict(size=5),
))
for x_val, label in [(2017, "Irma & Maria"), (2020, "COVID-19")]:
    fig.add_vline(x=x_val, line=dict(color="#aaa", width=1.5, dash="dash"),
                  annotation_text=label, annotation_position="top",
                  annotation_font=dict(size=11, color="#666"))

fig.update_layout(
    title="Accommodation and Food Services as Share of USVI GDP",
    yaxis_title="A&F share of nominal GDP (%)",
    yaxis_range=[0, 18],
    height=400,
    margin=dict(l=60, r=30, t=40, b=50),
    annotations=[dict(xref="paper", yref="paper", x=0, y=-0.10,
        text="<span style='color:#888;font-size:11px'>Source: BEA USVI GDP data. Coverage ends 2021. A&F ≠ tourism GDP.</span>",
        showarrow=False, xanchor="left")],
)
ch.save_fig(fig, "af-gdp-share", formats=("png",))
fig.show()
```

Accommodation and food services value added — the broadest BEA measure of the sector's economic contribution — fell from 13% of GDP in 2015 to 11.5% in 2017, collapsed to 6% in 2020, and rebounded to 11% in 2021, the last year BEA data are available. The rebound to 11% is encouraging but still below the pre-hurricane trend, and the GDP denominator during 2018–2021 likely reflects activity beyond the visitor economy. The sector had not returned to its pre-hurricane GDP share by 2021.

## Unresolved questions

This analysis surfaces several questions that the data alone cannot resolve:

**Why have overnight tourists not recovered to 2016 levels?** The hotel room deficit is real and constrains overnight capacity. Whether demand has also changed — in ways that would persist even if full capacity were restored — cannot be established from the available data. Possible factors worth investigating include the competitive position of other Caribbean destinations, traveler preference shifts following the pandemic, and long-term income effects from the post-hurricane period. These are open questions, not demonstrated findings.

**Is the VIIS NP recovery real?** The park exceeding its 2016 baseline while overnight tourists remain at 57% is a significant divergence. Either the park is drawing more visitors per overnight tourist (higher park utilization), or there is a visitor category being counted by NPS but not by USVIBER. This deserves direct investigation with NPS staff.

**What does 66% occupancy on a smaller room base actually mean for the economy?** High occupancy on reduced inventory may reflect healthy operating margins at surviving hotels while masking a smaller aggregate economic contribution. The Census 2022 data (1,650 accommodation employees vs. 3,876 in 2012) suggests the surviving hotel sector is operating at significantly reduced staffing levels.
